intro.data: Encoding here is TWO steps: first Encode the text, then Compress it — the only way to reach C. The way back is a single Decode that must undo BOTH steps at once and return the EXACT original. Bring the faithful Encode, Compress, and the true Decode from the tray onto the board and wire the round trip, leaving the garbling look-alikes behind. Among the three decoders, only one truly inverts the pair.
intro.alchemy: Transmuting here is TWO steps: Transmute the lead, then Condense it — the only path to C. The way back is a single Revert that must undo BOTH and return the EXACT original. Bring the faithful Transmute, Condense, and the true Revert from the tray onto the board and wire the round trip, leaving the look-alikes behind.
intro.spellcraft: Sealing here is TWO steps: Seal the sigil, then Fold it — the only path to C. The way back is a single Unseal that must undo BOTH and return the EXACT original. Bring the faithful Seal, Fold, and the true Unseal from the tray onto the board and wire the round trip, leaving the look-alikes behind.
intro.abstract: Values are concrete round-trip tokens: f sends 3 ↦ (3), g sends (3) ↦ ((3)), and the true decoder d sends ((3)) ↦ 3 — so the faithful round trip 3 → (3) → ((3)) → 3 returns the original. From the tray bring f, g, and d, wiring A back to A; the garbling look-alikes (which land on (5), ((8)), or 7) never bring 3 back. d = (g∘f)⁻¹.

afterSuccess.data: You encoded both steps and the single Decode restored the EXACT original — so Decode is the inverse of the whole two-step encoding: d ∘ (g∘f) = id. The inverse of a composite is one arrow that undoes it all. Look-alikes that lost or garbled anything failed.
afterSuccess.alchemy: You transmuted both steps and the single Revert restored the EXACT original: Revert is the inverse of the whole encoding. The inverse of a composite undoes it all at once.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: You sealed both steps and the single Unseal restored the EXACT original: Unseal is the inverse of the whole sealing. The inverse of a composite undoes it all at once.
afterSuccess.abstract: d ∘ (g∘f) = id_A, so d = (g∘f)⁻¹. A composite of isomorphisms is an isomorphism, and one inverse undoes the whole composite.

reveal.summary: If f : A→B and g : B→C are isomorphisms, so is g∘f : A→C, and its inverse is f⁻¹ ∘ g⁻¹ — a single arrow C→A that undoes both steps and restores the original exactly.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: decode(compress(encode(x))) === x — one decoder that reverses the whole pipeline.
